decisions.question: The self-contained gate (Rule 2: 'Every contract, ADR and OQ id the file names has its text inline in its section. Other phases' ids appear only in the Phase block's Dependencies and Collides with lines') flags ids that occur only inside verbatim excerpts. How does it apply, given S98's, S102's and S117's precedent? The set here: contract ids bus-api@v2, flutter-binding@v2, navigation-api@v1, nidana-checks@v1, topic-codegen@v1, topic-model@v1, topology-dsl@v2, topology-ir@v1; OQ ids OQ8, OQ9, OQ12, OQ-T2, OQ-F1; other-phase ids nidana.flutter.1 and nidana.model.1 to .6 outside Dependencies and Collides with. What differs from nidana.model.6: this phase's own Verification names topic-codegen@v1 and nidana-checks@v1 (they replay as PENDING until nidana.tooling's packages exist, while their structure and schema sets pass), where nidana.model.6's named topic-model@v1; and the Scope cites the node-local decision D2.

options.label: Apply the gate to ids the file selects; excerpt-internal citations stay as the source's words
options.consequence: Follows S98, S102 and S117. The file stays verbatim excerpts and template text; ADR-001 and ADR-002, the only ids at selected positions, are inline. The orchestrator's gate prints its one known warning (contract ids named without a Contracts subsection).

options.label: Add Contracts subsections for topic-codegen@v1 and nidana-checks@v1
options.consequence: Would inline two contracts' Interface and Guarantees for a phase that consumes and produces none, contradicting the Contracts selection rule (only those Consumes or Produces names) and handing the session text the replay tool never reads as Interface.

options.label: Paraphrase or drop the excerpt text that carries the ids
options.consequence: Breaks Rule 1 (verbatim, no truncation) and would hand the session a Scope or Verification that is not the plan's.

options.label: Stop and ask
options.consequence: Blocks the run on a question S98, S102 and S117 already answered the same way.

decisions.chosen: Apply the gate to ids the file selects; excerpt-internal citations stay as the source's words
decisions.why: Same reasoning as S98, S102 and S117: the Contracts and Open questions selection rules and Rule 1 cannot all hold under a reading of Rule 2 that counts every id inside a mandated excerpt. The two contract ids in this phase's Verification are a statement of what a replay of those contracts' fixtures shows while their implementing packages are absent (PENDING, with the structure and schema sets passing), not an Interface this phase implements. The phase's Scope states the whole behavior it builds (the file comparison, the recorded invocation with its path normalization, the restriction by declared ids, the single pub get before either set, PENDING for a command whose package is absent), and the fixtures those replays read are data under hsdd/contract/fixture/, which the tool reads at run time; its tests replay a stand-in generator in a temporary workspace. So nothing the implementer builds is missing from the file. D2 (cited in the Scope) is a node-local decision, not a contract, ADR or OQ id, so Rule 2 does not reach it and no rule selects it into the file; the behavior the Scope attaches to it (PENDING for a command whose package is absent) is stated in ADR-001 item 9, which is inline, as S102 already ruled for D2. A skill wording that scoped Rule 2 to selected ids, or told the writer to inline cited contracts, would have changed my mind.
